component.name: Packages
component.summary: Install and remove software on Aelum

description.p: Shows the packages this system chose — not their dependency trees — and removes them with their orphaned dependencies, showing what would break first. Browse searches every configured repository, installs with one click, and points out updates; an Aelum page lists the apps Aelum publishes that this system does not have yet; an AUR page searches the Arch User Repository and builds what you install on your own machine. Opening a .pkg.tar.zst file installs that too. Package transactions run as root through one polkit action and show pacman's own output.

ul.li: The window opens on the databases it already has: at start they are only re-fetched when they are more than ten minutes old. The Refresh button always checks.
The header's database date now survives closing the app, and an upgrade run through the app counts as a check.
The AUR update check's 'nothing newer' message now says no new versions were found for the packages it asked about - reworded in all 28 languages.
The AUR page can now check the AUR packages already on this system for newer versions: press Check and only names whose AUR version is newer are listed. Nothing is fetched from the AUR until you ask.
Corrected wording in all 28 translations — wrong terms, broken agreement, typos, and one concept carried by two different words inside the same locale.
The AUR list marks vote counts with a star instead of a triangle.

A transaction that was interrupted — closing the app during a download, or a killed pacman — no longer leaves the package database locked: the next refresh, install or removal works instead of failing with "unable to lock database".
Added an About dialog: the (i) button in the header shows the version and links.
The header now shows when the package databases were last refreshed.
The AUR page explains that AUR packages are community-published and unreviewed; hovering the vote count explains it.
Fixed the spacing above the package list on the Updates and Browse pages.

A request whose dependency is a virtual with several providers now asks which one to install — names, repositories and sizes listed, pacman's default preselected — instead of silently taking the first.
The transaction dialog gained a real progress bar with honest counts: download progress tracks what pacman has actually proven finished, and its output arrives as it is printed instead of at the end.
Packages installed as the answer to a provider question are marked as dependencies, so removing the package that needed them takes them back.
The transaction dialog stays compact and grows only while pacman's output is shown.
The list frame now ends at the bottom of the window: rows scroll inside a fixed outline instead of the outline running on to the end of the list.
The Installed and AUR tabs gained a gap between the search field and the list, matching Browse.
Build-only dependencies are now removed automatically after a package built from the AUR is installed.
AUR dependencies are installed as dependencies, not as explicit packages, so leftovers are recognized and removable when nothing needs them any more.
New AUR tab: search the AUR and install what you find. The PKGBUILD is downloaded, built on this machine, and the result installed
An AUR package's dependencies come from the repositories whenever a repository has one; only the AUR parts are built, and the whole install is one confirmation and one log
Nothing is fetched from the AUR until you search: the tab has no badge, and the app never asks the AUR on its own
Browsing no longer lists a package twice when its name is in more than one repository
A package now names the repository the system would actually install it from
While a database refresh runs, the tabs step aside and say so: "Databases refresh in progress, please wait…" — the rows behind it were the state before the check
The app now lists its own package, so it receives updates like any other; only its removal is refused.
The app icon now uses the standard package glyph from the system icon theme.
New Aelum tab: the distro's own apps your system doesn't have yet, with a dot when new ones are published
The app now speaks all 28 of the desktop's languages — interface, dialogs, and the launcher entry
Installs and updates now ask in words: Do you want to install <name> <version>?
Removing a package answers instantly: the confirmation used to appear about two seconds after the press
The confirmation asks one question and adds at most two facts: what still needs the package, and how many unneeded dependencies go along
The unneeded-dependency count follows pacman's -Rns rule and no longer counts unrelated leftovers
Sync databases are read as gzip or zstd, whichever the repository serves: Arch publishes them gzipped, so nothing was listed as updatable and Browse had no results
A database that cannot be read is reported instead of appearing as an empty list
The Updates tab moves after Browse, and the Installed page no longer repeats the update count the tab badge already shows
